$meta.title: OML lattice form — finite-trace σ-liftability
$meta.purpose: Zoom-out index of the OML/lattice attack. Load this first; follow detail pointers into the working note for proofs, scope, and session receipts.
$meta.what_is_it: Does every finitely additive two-valued state on a concrete σ-complete OML have each finite trace reproduced by some σ-additive two-valued state?
$meta.status: OPEN — conjectured latticehood implies Φ; no proof or OML counterexample.
$meta.the_shape: Φ is density of σ-additive states inside finitely additive states, not equality. Compact eligible local slices imply eventwise selection, so any bad face needs a noncompact slice. The 44-event centre-free five-block survivor is banked as a finite result. Its one-interval q0 inflation preserves exactly five maximal blocks, sigma-completeness, trivial centre, the proper C01 boundary, and a noncompact local slice at hand-proof level, but remains Phi-tame because its single fibre coordinate separates. A global 60-form truth-vector audit closes the compatibility-clique gap left by centralizer checks; the smallest P(2) triangle twist is either nonfaithful or gauge-trivial.

reductions.name: Finite-trace σ-liftability Φ
reductions.one_line: Φ(L): every finite trace realized by a global finitely additive two-valued state is realized by some global σ-additive two-valued state.

reductions.name: Φ as Stone density
reductions.one_line: Φ(L) iff St_σ(L) is dense in St_fa(L) inside {0,1}^L; equality of the two state spaces is not required.

reductions.name: General relational boundary descent
reductions.one_line: Phi is equivalent to choosing one finitely additive extension whose trace on every overlap-generated boundary admits a pattern-preserving local sigma lift; matching all lifts to that common trace makes them glue.

reductions.name: Genuine OML dense-nonopen boundary
reductions.one_line: A countable-coordinate sigma-field times MO2 is a concrete sigma-complete OML with two maximal blocks whose actual sigma-field boundary has dense nonopen point and sigma-liftable loci, already on a one-event face; one private Boolean generator suffices.

reductions.name: Compact local sigma-selection
reductions.one_line: If every eligible local sigma-state slice for a coherent finite face is compact, the face sigma-lifts: a global finitely additive witness makes every finite family of eventwise overlap equations solvable by local Dirac states. Thus every bad face has a noncompact eligible slice.

reductions.name: Irreducible boundary realization skeleton
reductions.one_line: Every two-block interface is central, but completing two crossed interfaces intervalwise produces a 56-event centre-free concrete sigma-complete OML with seven maximal blocks; every generated boundary equals its full block.

reductions.name: Seven-block common-base inflation dichotomy
reductions.one_line: A times L* is a concrete sigma-complete OML with exactly the seven inflated blocks, saturated boundaries, and face-exposed dense-nonopen local sigma topology, but its centre is A times {0,1}; every nontrivial common-base inflation is therefore reducible.

reductions.name: Distributed one-interval inflation
reductions.one_line: Replacing q0 by one Boolean fibre propagates through exactly B,D0,D1; the closure has seven maximal blocks, trivial centre, saturated boundaries, and a face-exposed noncompact sigma slice, but every finite face sigma-lifts by fibrewise replacement.

reductions.name: Two-fibre atom-substitution no-go
reductions.one_line: Every atom jointly chargeable with q0 has disjoint propagation support. The smallest pair occupies a five-cycle and closes as a centre-free seven-block OML, but its fibre relation is the full product, monodromy is identity, and independent point replacement proves Phi-tameness.

reductions.name: Two-block rescue
reductions.one_line: A coherent value-1 pattern supported in at most two blocks is Dirac-rescued; any witness needs at least three blocks.

mechanism_exclusions.name: Type-partition obstruction
mechanism_exclusions.one_line: Per-atom pairwise-disjointness sigma-kills over a localizer whose kill-type cells are events (automatic for countable atom families or locally full bases) contradict the finitely additive witness itself, block-free on any concrete sigma-class; disjointness is a finitely additive killer, so witness asymmetry must come from countable disjoint-union geometry or Ulam-type completeness failure.

mechanism_exclusions.name: No-Fubini value forcing
mechanism_exclusions.one_line: Two-valued sigma-additivity has no Fubini: any event persistently splitting a countably closed dichotomy base (e.g. any order event over the coarse box filter) is sigma-value-free over that marginal, so no witness can force coupling values through countable/co-countable marginal structure; forcing must use in-block countable disjoint-union geometry.

mechanism_exclusions.name: Pointwise-resolved overlap mechanism
mechanism_exclusions.one_line: If the set intersection of an intended incompatible pair is exhausted by L-events below it, latticehood forces compatibility (T1 second form), after which 2BR kills the pattern; realizations keeping the exhaustion visible lose latticehood by an omega1-chain of lower bounds.

mechanism_exclusions.name: Countable/co-countable fibre fence
mechanism_exclusions.one_line: A one-interval inflation is essentially irreducible iff its fibre algebra survives the countable quotient; ctble/coctble(omega1) fibres die there (quotient = the four-element Boolean algebra over the realized crossed half-traces, centre everything), so purely countable/co-countable coarse structure leaves the admissible class.

mechanism_exclusions.name: Jointly-generating transverse-overlap collapse

campaign_14_cells.one_line: A 56-event centre-free OML realizes the full off-face relation; its fixed-interface concrete closure preserves the diagonal through three cells with pair-local repairs.

campaign_15_closure.name: Arbitrary-index one-hub tameness
campaign_15_closure.one_line: The fixed-interface support-two family is sigma-complete with Stfa=Stsigma for every nonempty index set, hence satisfies Phi.

campaign_15_closure.name: Bipartite crossed-rectangle cut
campaign_15_closure.one_line: The stripped K22/K23/K32 grouped coordinate closures remain nonlattices; opposite edges have incomparable rectangle bounds.

campaign_16_rectangle.name: Full conditional two-by-two rectangle failure
campaign_16_rectangle.one_line: The 198-event full conditional grid closes orthogonally to 230 events while preserving its exact relations, but retains two incomparable rectangle upper bounds.

campaign_16_rectangle.name: Iterated stripped rectangle repairs
campaign_16_rectangle.one_line: Two explicit repair branches give 1296- and 3456-event concrete OMLs, both reconstructing Bool(q0,q1); all-branch distributed-preserving completion remains open.

campaign_17_macro_completion.name: K22 macro-completion reconstruction
campaign_17_macro_completion.one_line: Every concrete OML subfamily of P(2^4) containing the four K22 edge algebras reconstructs Bool(q0,q1) or Bool(r0,r1).

campaign_18_fine_fibre.name: Two-depth fine-fibre rectangle repairs
campaign_18_fine_fibre.one_line: Whole classes of 64/128 points and a secondary four-point class repair successive joins without side reconstruction or activation collapse, but all closures remain nonlattices.

campaign_19_terminal_reduction.name: Fixed-carrier fine-repair termination
campaign_19_terminal_reduction.one_line: Every unrestricted repair chain on the finite full-grid carrier terminates at a finite concrete OML, and every same-carrier completion contains such a terminal.

campaign_19_terminal_reduction.name: T-FIN terminal dichotomy
campaign_19_terminal_reduction.one_line: Does every full-grid repair terminal reconstruct one same-side Boolean boundary or create a nonzero activation-supported event?

campaign_19_terminal_reduction.name: Coordinate-closed completion reconstruction
campaign_19_terminal_reduction.one_line: Every full-grid completion whose profile-measurable pairs have profile-measurable joins reconstructs Bool(q0,q1) or Bool(r0,r1).

campaign_19_terminal_reduction.name: Non-profile fibre-splitter incidence
campaign_19_terminal_reduction.one_line: Bare residue squares do not collapse, but profile-join-hull closure forces a P(16) completion and reconstruction; a preserving terminal must sustain a certificate-relevant nonevent hull.

external_sufficient_conditions.name: Finite carriers
external_sufficient_conditions.one_line: Finite carriers satisfy Φ because finite and countable additivity coincide.

external_sufficient_conditions.name: Horizontal sums
external_sufficient_conditions.one_line: Horizontal-sum-like carriers lie in the known tame region, though they do not exhaust concrete irreducible OMLs.

external_sufficient_conditions.name: Finite-interface quarantine
external_sufficient_conditions.one_line: Lean proves that finite raw overlap families at every maximal block force every finitely coherent pattern to have a global sigma-additive two-valued extension; the equivalent finite generated-boundary formulation remains an elementary hand step.

external_sufficient_conditions.name: Single pullback with common-point extension
external_sufficient_conditions.one_line: A one-edge A-D-C compatibility system is Phi-tame when every coherent finite endpoint trace admits sigma-additive endpoint extensions over one common D state; graph shape alone is insufficient.
